newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-ZAGALLO LEAVES FRANCE IN TRIUMPHANT MOOD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZAGALLO LEAVES FRANCE IN TRIUMPHANT MOOD.

text.p: Mario Zagallo left France on Tuesday convinced his Brazilian side, unbeaten in the Tournoi de France after ending it with a 1-0 victory over tournament winners England, can retain the World Cup next year.

"We didn't lose and you saw the tactical change we made. We won 1-0, you have to respect the green-yellow (colours)," Brazil's coach said in a brief news conference before his team flew home with the Copa America their next objective.

"It was important to face three great selections. This was a very good preparation for the Copa America. The Copa is an important tournament but this is the one from which we can draw conclusions for next year."
The Copa America in Bolivia begins on Wednesday, but Brazil do not play their first match until Friday.

"We've found a better tactical game to face the Europeans than we had before. This was our best 90 minutes of the tournament," said Zagallo, whose side also draw 1-1 with hosts France and 3-3 with Italy.
"Tonight we had a compactness in defence, midfield and attack, but you can't compare this team with 1994. It has a different game and this is a different tournament."
Zagallo was Carlos Alberto Parreira's assistant when Brazil won their fourth World Cup in the United States three years ago.
England coach Glenn Hoddle went along with Zagallo's assessment and said the match was another learning experience for his players.
"They are the best creative players in the world and have proved that over the years," Hoddle said.
"We were a little bit fatigued, we defended well and pressed them in the first half.

"I was pleased with the way we handled their front line, but we need better balance. We didn't get forward quite quickly enough," Hoddle said after one defensive sip let in Romario for a slick winning goal on the hour.
"There's still a gap to be breached but we do have things they don't," added Hoddle, whose side won the tournament by one point from the Brazilians after impressive wins over France and Italy.
